draft.title: Young people and tax
card: A young person who starts a job needs a tax file number (TFN). It is a personal number that the tax office uses to keep track of their tax.
The employer takes tax out of each pay and sends it to the government. The worker receives the pay that is left.
The tax year ends on 30 June. After that date, workers lodge a tax return, which tells the tax office what they earned and what tax was paid.
If too much tax was taken out during the year, the worker may get some money back as a refund.
draft.remember: Get a TFN, let your employer take tax from your pay, then lodge a return after 30 June to see if you get some back.

a.q: Why might a teenager who works part time get money back after lodging a tax return?
opts: Their employer may have taken out too much tax
The government pays all workers a bonus each year
They did not need a tax file number to start work
Their employer paid their tax before they were hired
a.why: Tax is taken from each pay, and if too much was taken out over the year, the worker may get a refund. A bonus is not paid to every worker.
a.clue: Think about what is taken from each pay during the year.

b.q: Noah, aged 15, starts a job at a bakery in Perth. What should he do first so his tax can be recorded?
opts: Give his employer his tax file number
Wait until 30 June to lodge a tax return
Ask his employer to keep all of his pay
Send his pay slips to the bakery's customers
b.why: A young worker needs a tax file number so the tax office can keep track of their tax. Lodging a return happens after 30 June, not before starting.
b.clue: It is a personal number linked to the tax office.

a.best: Their employer may have taken out too much tax

b.best: Give his employer his tax file number

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a qualifier ('may') and it echoes the card's wording ('too much tax was taken out'). The other options are plainly absurd, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
The clue ('a personal number linked to the tax office') points straight at the only option that mentions a number, which gives the answer away.
The card says a young worker needs a TFN but never says the worker gives it to the employer. The question asks for that step without the card teaching it.

proposal.title: Young people and tax
card: A young person who starts a job needs a tax file number (TFN). It is a personal number that the tax office uses to keep track of their tax.
When they start the job, the worker gives their TFN to their employer. The employer then takes tax out of each pay and sends it to the government.
The tax year ends on 30 June. After that date, the worker lodges their own tax return, which tells the tax office what they earned and what tax was paid.
If the tax taken from their pay was more than the tax they owed for the year, the worker may get the difference back as a refund.
proposal.remember: Your employer takes tax from each pay, and your tax return after 30 June can show whether you paid too much.

a.q: Why might a teenager who works part time get money back after lodging a tax return?
opts: More tax came out of their pay than they owed for the year
Their employer took no tax at all out of their pay that year
They gave their employer their tax file number when hired
They lodged their tax return early, before the 30 June date
a.why: A refund is the difference when the tax taken from pay is more than the tax owed. If no tax was taken out, there would be nothing to give back. Giving a TFN to an employer is a normal step, not a reason for a refund.
a.clue: Compare what was taken from pay with what was owed.

b.q: Noah, aged 15, starts a job at a bakery in Perth. What should he do with his tax file number when he starts?
opts: Give it to the bakery so tax can be taken from his pay
Keep it to himself until he lodges a tax return in July
Use it to pay his own tax to the tax office each week
Give it to the bakery so it can lodge his tax return
b.why: A new worker gives their TFN to their employer, and the employer takes tax from each pay. The bakery does not lodge Noah's return for him: he lodges his own after 30 June.
b.clue: Who takes the tax out of each pay, and who lodges the return?

b.best: Give it to the bakery so tax can be taken from his pay
